key_insight: The paper introduces a smooth, explicit elastoplastic-damage update that uses closed-form, history-based branches to preserve irreversible plasticity and damage without a local Newton solve.
engineering_relevance: It is useful for graphics and real-time solid simulation because it favors simple, vectorizable implementation and stable history evolution over exact yield-surface enforcement.
method: Softplus generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain, then a max-history projection enforces irreversibility.
A deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction, while an exponential scalar variable drives damage degradation.
Active and frozen branches are evaluated analytically from one response energy, avoiding local nonlinear solves.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the method on 1D cyclic tension, 2D cantilever bending, 3D platen compression, and a torus, and report branchwise energy-gradient agreement, residual deformation, and mesh-resolution sensitivity.
watch_item: The approach is intended for isotropic, proportional or nearly proportional loading; it degrades sharply under path changes and is not a substitute for general return mapping or anisotropic damage models.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
